additions.definition: A tool that cuts open a food can, commonly using a cutting wheel. A bottle-opening attachment does not make all bottle openers can openers.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

additions.definition: A vessel with electrical water heating and a pouring spout. Adjustable temperature and gooseneck pouring are model features, not requirements of every electric kettle.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

additions.definition: A rotating basket within a bowl removes water from washed salad leaves. Its basket may drain like a colander, but the spinning assembly is a distinct tool.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

additions.definition: A pressing tool that extracts juice by compressing citrus halves. This identity covers the press, not every reamer or powered fruit juicer.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

additions.definition: A brush for spreading liquids such as egg wash, syrup or melted butter over food. Bristle material and heat tolerance depend on the actual brush.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

relationships.note: Transfers a liquid coating to food.

additions.definition: A transfer tool with a broad receiving opening and narrower outlet for filling containers. A strainer may be added; filtering is not inherent to every funnel.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

additions.definition: A hand-operated mill pushes soft food through a perforated disc. It can separate skins or seeds while making puree, unlike a blender that cuts the mixture together.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

relationships.note: Passing soft food through a disc makes puree.

additions.definition: An electrical appliance that dries food using heat and circulating air. Capacity and airflow arrangement vary; the appliance alone does not establish a safe preservation procedure.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

relationships.note: Heat and airflow remove moisture; this is not a preservation guarantee.

additions.definition: A handled set of blades or wires for cutting solid fat into dry ingredients. It is a hand tool, distinct from a powered jug blender.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

relationships.note: A manual fat-cutting tool, not a powered liquid blender.

additions.definition: A heat-retaining baking surface that transfers oven heat to the base of dough. Bread and flatbreads are other uses; a metal baking steel is a different material.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

relationships.note: A heated baking surface for dough.

additions.definition: A mill or powered blade tool intended to grind spices. The documented electric example also grinds nuts; that capability is not assumed for every grinder.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

additions.definition: A hand press that forces cooked potato through perforations. It can also process suitable soft fruit or vegetables; it differs mechanically from pounding with a masher.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

relationships.note: Pressing through holes differs from crushing with a masher.

additions.definition: A pressure vessel designed to process jars for home canning. Small pressure cookers are not interchangeable with the equipment used to establish canning schedules.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

relationships.note: Canning schedules are not transferable to small pressure cookers.

additions.definition: A deep, lidded vessel with a rack for processing jars submerged in boiling water. This is distinct from a pressure canner; use a validated procedure for the food.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

relationships.note: Atmospheric boiling-water processing and pressure processing are distinct.

additions.definition: A gripping tool for lifting canning jars while keeping them upright. Its jar-holding shape distinguishes it from general serving tongs.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

additions.definition: In pastry work, build distinct dough and fat layers through rolling and folding. Folding a mixture or merely stacking ingredients does not necessarily laminate pastry.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

relationships.note: Pastry lamination builds dough and fat layers; not every fold does.

additions.definition: Prick dough with small holes to let steam escape and limit unwanted puffing during baking. This pastry purpose is narrower than general piercing.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

relationships.note: Dough puncturing has a specific baking purpose.

additions.definition: Prepare a whole bird by removing its backbone and opening it flat. This is a poultry-specific preparation, not complete deboning or every form of butterflying.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

relationships.note: Opening poultry flat does not remove every bone.

additions.definition: Separate the fat of butter from its milk solids and watery component. Merely melting butter does not complete clarification.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

relationships.note: Melting does not itself separate all butter components.

additions.definition: Remove suspended material from stock or broth to obtain a clearer liquid, as for consomme. This is distinct from separating butterfat.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

relationships.note: Clearing broth and separating butterfat involve different materials.

additions.definition: Hydrate gelatine in cold liquid before dissolving it into the preparation. This use of bloom is separate from heating spices or wetting coffee.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

additions.definition: Soften fruit by resting it with sugar or liquid. Sugar draws juice from the fruit; added liquid can also carry flavour. This entry concerns culinary fruit preparation.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

additions.definition: Salt food in advance of cooking without immersing it in a prepared salt-water bath. This seasoning technique is not a guarantee of preservation or a substitute for a validated curing method.
additions.uncertainties: Broader synonyms and model-specific operational claims are not inferred.

relationships.note: Direct salting differs from immersion in prepared brine.

improvements.added: A processor can leave deliberately coarse pieces or use a disc to slice and shred. A blender is usually chosen for a flowing, smooth mixture. Overlapping puree tasks do not make the appliances equivalent; use the attachment and batch size the recipe actually needs.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: A blade chops material already in the bowl, whereas a slicing disc cuts food as it enters. Choosing a disc instead of running the bowl blade changes the kind of result, not just its fineness. Blender recipes with plentiful liquid may need a different work-bowl limit.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: Tilt-head and bowl-lift describe how the bowl and mixing head are accessed, not different culinary processes. Optional pasta rollers and grinders are separate attachments: having a stand mixer does not by itself provide those functions.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: The basket supports food above the water while allowing steam through; a lid and suitable pan complete the cooking arrangement. A colander can drain food, but that alone does not establish that it fits a covered pan or is suitable for heating.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: The measurement location matters as much as the display. An appliance thermometer describes the surrounding cooking environment; a food probe describes the region around its sensing area. These readings answer different questions, so an oven reading does not replace a measurement within the food.
improvements.uncertainties: USDA refetch returned 403; restricted to existing sourced project evidence.

improvements.added: A pressure-canner reference describes equipment and a validated jar-processing system. A pressure-cooker recipe describes cooking a meal. Similar pressure-related names do not transfer one system’s evidence to the other; choose the applicable documentation before treating them as substitutes.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: Thin, repeated vegetable slices are useful in fermented-vegetable preparation as well as salads. Slicing and pounding have different jobs: a slicer sets piece shape, while pounding or massaging releases juice. A uniform cut alone does not establish fermentation conditions.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: Stir-fry ingredients are often added in stages because they need different cooking times. A wok provides space for that sequence, but the vessel name does not make a crowded mixture a stir-fry. Match the preparation and loading to the intended method.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: The covered stage of a braise retains moisture; reducing its cooking liquid is a separate, evaporative step. A Dutch oven can participate in both, but keeping the same lid position throughout does not serve both purposes.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: Skillet describes the shallow cooking form; cast iron describes the material. A cast-iron Dutch oven is a deeper, lidded vessel. Shared material does not make their capacity, access for turning food or evaporation behaviour identical.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: A simmer describes the liquid’s activity, while reduction describes losing liquid through evaporation. A covered simmer can cook food without the same reduction as an uncovered pan. State the desired consistency separately when a sauce must also concentrate.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: Boiling food immerses it in hot liquid; steaming exposes it to vapour above liquid. These are different heat-transfer arrangements even when both begin with boiling water. A steamer basket therefore does not make its contents boiled food.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: Covering a roasting vessel changes how moisture escapes and introduces a trapped-steam environment. Browning an exposed surface and retaining moisture under a lid are different aims; a recipe may deliberately move between them.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: A covered cooking stage and an uncovered sauce-finishing stage can belong to the same dish. Removing the lid encourages evaporation; this explains why the sauce may be reduced separately after the food is tender.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: Kneading develops a dough’s structure; pastry lamination preserves distinct layers of dough and fat through rolling and folding. Both involve working dough, but continuous mixing is not a substitute for the layer-building operation.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: Adding a thickener and evaporating water can both change consistency, but they do not do the same work. Reduction removes liquid rather than adding body to it. A recipe’s target volume and its texture cue should therefore be read together.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: Deep poaching fully surrounds the food with cooking liquid. The liquid can contribute flavour through stock, aromatics or wine, while a serving sauce may be prepared separately. Poaching does not require turning all of the cooking liquid into the final sauce.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: Surface scoring and dough docking both make openings, but docking uses small punctures to limit puffing. Do not treat a decorative or expansion-guiding slash as equivalent to pricking the dough across its surface.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: Docking controls puffing by making small holes; blind-baking cooks an empty pastry case. They can occur together, but one is a preparation and the other a baking stage. Docking a crust does not mean that it has already been blind-baked.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

improvements.added: Fermentation names the microbial transformation, not a promise that living organisms remain in the finished food. Later processing can change that. The process name alone does not establish a product’s storage conditions or a health benefit.
improvements.uncertainties: Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

Current IDs already cover these techniques; proof is accepted by prove. No additional synonym inferred for sous-vide cook.
Existing temper-chocolate/eggs/spices and scoped new clarification/gelatine entries preserve senses. No universal alias.
Cold smoking needs dedicated safety review; flash-fry lacks a sufficiently stable boundary for this batch; dry-brine is only pre-cooking seasoning here.

deferred.decision: Narrower or overlapping existing concept; defer names
deferred.reason: Compare scraper, thermometer, grater/zester, blowtorch and pasta-machine. Brand, sensing format and roller-only scope are not blanket aliases.
Distinct candidates not implemented in this batch; detailed source/scope review remains. Vacuum packaging is not a preservation guarantee.
No equivalence with metal-griddle, clay-casserole or oven asserted. Need regional educational evidence covering materials, shape, heat source and equipment-versus-dish senses.
Added pressure-canner, water-bath-canner and jar-lifter; no generic catch-all alias.
